scope: The OOVS L1 Foundational baseline: ten testable requirements, machine-readable catalogue, acceptance tests, assessment format, external mappings, governance, and validation assets.

validation.summary: Schemas, cross-file semantics, Markdown/JSON requirement parity, positive and expected-failure fixtures, local links, and manifest hashes all validated.

quality_checks.name: JSON Schema conformance
quality_checks.evidence: All schemas validate as Draft 2020-12 and every canonical example validates against its schema.

quality_checks.name: Requirement and test coverage
quality_checks.evidence: Ten requirements each map to exactly one acceptance test, with unique identifiers and ordered ordinals.

quality_checks.name: Markdown and machine-readable parity
quality_checks.evidence: Each requirement heading, objective, and normative statement matches requirements.json.

quality_checks.name: Expected-failure fixtures
quality_checks.evidence: Five negative fixtures fail validation for their declared reasons.

quality_checks.name: Assessment result semantics
quality_checks.evidence: Result states, applicability rules, evidence requirements, dates, and overall outcome are enforced.

quality_checks.name: Documentation links
quality_checks.evidence: All local Markdown links resolve inside the repository.

quality_checks.name: Safety review of published material
quality_checks.evidence: All examples and fixtures are synthetic and contain no personal, case, victim, credential, or operational data.

compatibility.identifier_stability: Requirement identifiers follow OOVS-v0.1.0-NN and acceptance tests follow OOVS-v0.1.0-TNN. They are stable within the 0.1 line; later versions may add identifiers without renumbering published ones.

scope_notes: This release defines the L1 Foundational baseline; additional assurance depth and profiles follow implementation evidence.
The synthetic assessment demonstrates the result format and does not represent an operational assessment.
External mappings are high-level relationships; clause-level crosswalks are published after primary-source and specialist review.
OIG and OTTM ship as 0.1 preview assets and are outside the normative OOVS result.
An OOVS assessment records a defined scope and result; it is not certification, accreditation, or a determination of legal compliance.
